commentary: The book is flat today with $982 in cash, and the market itself is in good shape (the S&P is well above its 200-day average). Five names on my watchlist hit their own buy triggers this morning, and I checked every one with fresh news - Okta, CrowdStrike, Datadog and GE Aerospace all either moved the wrong way today or simply haven't confirmed their setups yet, and Arista came within a hair of its breakout level but without the trading volume to confirm it, so I'm holding the line rather than chasing an unconfirmed touch. The one name that did clear a genuinely high bar was Micron: it reported an extraordinary quarter this morning, including about $100 billion of newly-disclosed contracted future revenue and billions in customer cash deposits to lock in memory chip supply that's sold out through next year - yet the stock still trades far cheaper than its peers. I started a small position there, sized conservatively since I'm buying into today's price jump rather than a settled base. What would change my mind: if Micron's move reverses hard on volume in the next few sessions, or if Arista and GE Aerospace actually confirm their setups with real volume behind the move - both are within a point or two of my stated levels and stay at the top of my watchlist.

proposal.thesis: Micron just delivered one of the cleanest beat-and-raise prints in the AI-supplier cohort: Q3 FY26 revenue of $41.5B (guided next quarter to $50B, +20% QoQ) with gross margin at 85% and guided to ~86%, an EPS beat of 24% ($25.11 vs $20.20 est). The company disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements worth roughly $100B of minimum contracted revenue, including $18B of customer cash deposits to secure HBM supply that is sold out through 2026 with demand outstripping supply by 50-67%. Despite the print and today's +12% reaction, the stock still trades at just 5.5-6.8x forward earnings versus a 30.6x semiconductor sector median, and the balance sheet is a fortress (net cash ~$23.75B, debt/equity 0.06, TTM FCF $26.2B). The setup is a post-earnings-drift trade, not a chase into an unresolved binary: the print already happened and the thesis is that the market has not yet re-rated the multiple to reflect the newly-disclosed, quantified demand visibility.

proposal.risk_map: Primary risk is that today's post-earnings pop is the whole move (sell-the-news chase) rather than the start of a re-rating drift; memory is a historically boom-bust cyclical and the market may simply not extend the multiple regardless of the backlog. A DRAM/NAND pricing air-pocket, a hyperscaler pausing HBM orders, or a broader semi-sector de-rating (the chips_crack_20 stress scenario) would hit this position hard given its 8.4% ATR. Sized at roughly half the normal risk budget given the momentum-factor unwind flag, and the stop is set at 1.4x ATR (11.8%) to survive ordinary post-earnings volatility, without an options expected-move cross-check since MU was outside this run's deep-research focus set.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: Sell-side is already bullish (Strong Buy, KeyBanc $1,750 PT, ~$1,490 mean target) yet MU still trades at just 5.5-6.8x forward earnings, an ~82% discount to the 30.6x semiconductor sector median. MY VIEW: the market is still pricing this as a garden-variety boom-bust memory cycle rather than a structurally-scarce, multi-year HBM supercycle. MECHANISM: today's print disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements worth ~$100B of MINIMUM CONTRACTED revenue, including $18B of customer CASH DEPOSITS to secure supply - a quantified, non-slideware signal of demand visibility that historical memory cycles never had, and which the stock's cyclical-discount multiple has not yet re-rated to reflect even after today's pop. RESOLUTION: the FY26 Q4 print (~2026-09-22, guided $50B revenue / ~$31 EPS / ~86% gross margin) and any HBM4/customer-agreement follow-on news over the next 30-45 days will show whether the backlog converts as guided; if it does, the multiple re-rates further even without new news.

closed_trades.thesis: HPE is the most valuation-protected way to own the AI-server/networking buildout in a tape where reaccelerating inflation (CPI 4.27%) and a rising 10-year (4.56%) are punishing rich multiples. It trades at just ~12.2x forward earnings and 1.67x sales - the cheapest in the server group - after a record fiscal Q2 and the completed Juniper acquisition, which adds a scaled networking franchise. Sell-side has responded with a +40.5% 30-day upward EPS revision, yet the stock is consolidating (1m +1.4%) and sits 23.8% below its 52-week high, so estimates are rising while price has not re-rated. The same SMCI collapse (-29%) that helps Dell consolidates enterprise AI-server demand toward HPE as customers de-risk suppliers. With the last print already behind it (38 days ago) and no earnings inside the 40-day window, this is a clean cheap-re-rating swing.

Dell is the best risk/reward in an extended AI-server complex: it pairs elite momentum (+143% 3m, +202% 6m) with the cheapest valuation in the group (forward P/E ~20.9, P/S 2.2) and a constructive entry, having pulled back only 2.2% from its 20-day high while sitting 4.1% off its 52-week high near a buy point. The 29% collapse in Super Micro is a direct tailwind, consolidating enterprise/AI-server share toward Dell as customers de-risk suppliers. Q1 fundamentals (revenue $23.4B, net income $965M) confirm profitable scale, and the current tape ('Dell Stock Nears Buy Point') shows institutional demand building. With no earnings until 9/3, a 45-day swing captures the momentum leg without event risk.

** `market_news` reported fetching 119 items (yahoo 49, cnbc 30, marketwatch 10, alpaca 30) and surfaced **15**, and because the cap keeps the *most recent* headlines, all 15 were published in the final 30 minutes before the gather — four of them the identical "12 [Sector] Stocks Moving In Tuesday's After-Market Session" template. The result is that the entire macro narrative of the session was dropped: not one headline about the US–Iran strikes that have crude up 6.55% in five sessions, and consequently `market_events.flags.counts.geopolitical` scored **0** on a night with a ten-day ceasefire proposal live. A required regime input returned a confident false negative, and I only caught it because I ran outside web research. Two cheap fixes: (1) **stratify the headline cap** — reserve half the slots for market-wide/macro stories and half for single-name, instead of sorting purely by recency; (2) **collapse templated Benzinga movers lists** ("N [Sector] Stocks Moving In...") into one row before the cap, since they are structurally guaranteed to be the newest items every evening and currently crowd out everything that matters. Secondary, and cheaper still: nothing in the bundle told me *where* today's money went — `momentum_health` correctly flagged "unwind" but a one-line leadership-rotation read (top and bottom sectors by same-day move) would have handed me the single most important fact of this session instead of my having to reconstruct it from 186 individual `pct_change_1d` fields.

** The three ideas that actually competed for capital this run — UNH, TRV and MPC — are all *non-focus* names, so the bundle gave me a numeric scan row and nothing else: no candlestick chart, no options-implied expected move, no `stop_engineering` floor, no `ownership_flow`, no insider read. I had to judge UNH's entry geometry against a 200-week moving average I could not see on a chart, and I have no idea whether its options market is leaning the way GS's is. This is adopted lesson LP-8200625986 recurring verbatim, and today it was the *deciding* constraint rather than a nuisance: the scanner should promote the top 2–3 non-focus `top_setups` rows (or any name carrying a >5% 30-day upward EPS revision) into the focus set each run so they receive a chart plus the deep bundle. As it stands, the moment leadership rotates out of my 13 focus names — which is precisely what a momentum unwind *is* — my research depth rotates out with it.

** the watchlist trigger checker is **direction-blind**, and that is what produced this run's false positive. My published PANW condition was a *reclaim* of ~$345 that *holds*; the alert fired because price came within 2% of $345 **from below** (live $340.12, -2.45% on the day) — the opposite of the stated condition. This is the same class of defect as LP-4566902391 (the AMD alert firing 3.9% off the level). Fix: parse a relation token out of `would_buy_at` — "reclaim / above / breaks out / closes above" requires price **at or above** the level, "pullback to / near / dip to / below" requires price **at or below** — and only fire when the relation is satisfied, defaulting to proximity-only with an explicit `relation: unknown` tag when no token parses. Secondary, same block: the alert quoted PANW's stale 7/20 close ($348.66) while `live_prices.json`, written four minutes earlier, carried $340.12 — the alert rows should quote the same live mark the `trigger_run_note` claims to have confirmed on, or the two blocks will keep contradicting each other on exactly the days a trigger matters.

** The `holdings_watchlist` depth scanned exactly 10 names, and two of the twelve focus names — GS and KKR — arrived as tape/8-K promotions with *no scan row at all*: no ATR, no RSI, no trend labels, no chart, no anchored VWAP. GS carries the second-strongest 30-day EPS revisions in the entire universe screen (+18.75%) and `institutions_buying_price_weak`, and I had to shelve it purely because I could not place an honest stop or judge entry geometry. This is the same defect logged as LP-8200625986 on 2026-07-19 for MU, still unfixed: **tape/8-K promotions should inherit the full scan row (ATR, trend, volume signal, anchored VWAP) and a chart, not just news and fundamentals** — otherwise the promotion mechanism surfaces names it cannot let me underwrite, which is worse than not surfacing them. Second, smaller: my own CRWD trigger was conditioned on a confirmed MACD bull cross, an indicator this system's own 12-year study measured at −0.01pp. Nothing flagged the contradiction between a stored watchlist trigger and a knowledge-base finding that retired the indicator — a cheap check comparing trigger text against measured-dead indicators would have caught it a week ago.
